issues.failure_explanation: For the stated coefficients, sigma*sigma^T = sigma^2 diag((x^i)^2), which vanishes whenever some coordinate x^i = 0 and whose smallest eigenvalue tends to 0, so there is no kappa>0 with xi^T(sigma sigma^T)xi >= kappa|xi|^2 for all (t,x) in [0,T]xR^d. Assumption 1(ii) and Assumption assumptionpde(i) (uniform ellipticity) therefore fail for this model; assumptionpde(ii) also fails since b(s,x)=rx and sigma(s,x)=sigma*diag(x) are unbounded, hence not C_b^1 in x. The claim that the assumptions hold for the Black-Scholes game put is thus false.

issues.failure_explanation: Ekeland's principle yields a maximizer of l(u) - (eta/delta) d(u,u_eta) with d a metric (linear in distance); the squared Euclidean distance is not a metric (it violates the triangle inequality), so the cited theorem does not provide a maximizer of the quadratically perturbed function l_eta. The perturbation Ekeland does provide is non-differentiable at its center and cannot serve as the C^{1,2} test function required in the subsequent viscosity argument; in addition, the proof never verifies that the maximizer lies in the interior of K, which is needed for V^lambda - phi_eta to have a genuine local minimum. Case 2 of Proposition apb1 is therefore unproven as written.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: It is easy to see that \eqref{scheme} implies the implicit discretization scheme \eqref{discretization}

issues.failure_explanation: Run backward from the terminal condition, the scheme first fixes Z_{t_i} explicitly and then requires solving the implicit scalar equation y = c + f_lambda(t_i, X^tilde, y, Z_{t_i}) Delta t. Unique solvability needs a contraction-type condition such as K_y Delta t < 1, which is never assumed: the hypotheses impose only Delta t < 1/(16 K_z^2), which constrains nothing when K_z = 0 and in any case does not control K_y Delta t. Within the stated hypotheses the equation can have multiple solutions: e.g. f(t,x,y,z)=|y| (K_y=1, K_z=0), constant barriers p_b=-10, p_w=10, g=-3, Delta t=2, lambda=3, where y = -3 + 2|y| has both roots y=3 and y=-1 in the admissible region. The scheme's output is thus not well defined as stated.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Add the standard smallness condition (e.g. K_y Delta t < 1, under which the fixed-point map is contractive in the middle region and monotone in the penalty regions), or specify a selection rule among solutions of the implicit equation.
issues.overall_effect: The paper's central algorithm can be multi-valued on coarse grids within the stated parameter regime. The error theorems are stated for any triple satisfying the scheme equations, so their bounds are not directly falsified, but the scheme's input-output contract fails.
issues.title: Implicit backward step of the two-grid scheme is not verified to be single-valued
issues.why_classification: A standard local condition (or a selection rule) restores well-definedness with no change to any bound, rate, or advertised scope; the asymptotic regime of interest is unaffected.

Absorbing the standalone Delta t term (and lambda^2 Delta t-tilde) into C_2 lambda^2 Delta t requires Delta t <= lambda^2 Delta t, i.e. lambda >= 1, which is not assumed: the hypotheses allow any lambda > 2 K_y, and when K_y < 1/2 one may take lambda < 1. issues.failure_explanation: Equation (rterm1new) bounds the driver-regularity part of E[|E[r_i|F_{t_i}]|] by C_2(Delta t^{3/2} + integral of E|Y^lambda_s - Y^lambda_{t_i}| ds over [t_i,t_{i+1}]), but (rtermn) asserts a per-interval bound containing only Delta t^{3/2}, silently discarding the Y^lambda-increment term.
